To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a parallel cascaded architecture that operates in parallel over time can outperform a conventional serial architecture in terms of both accuracy and speed; 2) the cascaded architecture can be trained with a temporal-difference loss to improve performance; and 3) the architecture can be used to generate a time-varying trace of predictions that can be used for a variety of purposes, including improving information processing and inference.

(1) a parallel, cascaded architecture with a temporal-difference loss improves anytime prediction over standard methods, (2) the cascaded architecture has interesting properties, such as being more robust to noise than a standard network and being more accurate for typical than atypical inputs, and (3) the cascaded network's output can be exploited to enhance information processing and inference.

(i) a cascaded ResNet architecture that incorporates temporal-difference training outperforms a conventional ResNet in a variety of settings, including anytime prediction, and (ii) the architecture exhibits intriguing properties, including the ability to classify typical instances faster than atypical instances, and the ability to provide a signal that can improve information processing and prediction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of deep neural network architectures with cascaded dynamics, and the analysis of the properties of the resulting models.
the design of deep networks that are more like biological brains than are conventional deep networks, and we show that such networks have desirable properties.
the design and analysis of a new deep network that exhibits cascaded parallel dynamics.

the proposed architecture is a novel, effective, and biologically-inspired anytime-prediction method.
the parallel cascaded architecture is an important step toward a biologically plausible model that achieves state-of-the-art performance on the task of anytime prediction.
our cascaded architecture outperforms state-of-the-art methods on a variety of tasks and is a step forward in our understanding of the role of temporal dynamics in deep learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we introduce a novel cascaded architecture and a novel temporal-difference loss function, which together enable anytime predictions that improve over time and are robust to both persistent noise and transient noise.
we propose a biologically-inspired architecture, which we call the cascaded ResNet, that improves the speed-accuracy trade-off for image classification.
we propose a new architecture, the Cascaded ResNet, and show how it can be used to improve anytime prediction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of neural networks are an important design parameter that can be exploited for improved performance.
the dynamics of a neural network architecture can be a powerful tool for improving the performance of deep networks.
anytime prediction is not only possible but also beneficial in a cascaded architecture.
